rationale: Heston and Sadka (2010, JFQA) is an empirical cross-sectional/international asset-pricing paper. It has an explicit Data section (Section II, page 2-3: FactSet monthly stock returns including dividends and market capitalizations for 14 non-U.S. countries, January 1985-June 2006, 258 months, 2,440,681 firm-month observations; returns measured in U.S. dollars). Methodology is fully operationalized: (1) monthly cross-sectional regressions of returns on country dummies plus a single lagged return, lags k = 1-12 and every 12th lag through 60, OLS and heteroskedasticity-adjusted WLS (eq. 1, Table 2); (2) decile-spread portfolio strategies sorted on historical returns in excess of equal-weighted local country indices, with annual (lags that are multiples of 12) vs nonannual lag groupings for Year 1, Years 2-3, and Years 4-5, EW and VW, with intra-/intercountry return decomposition (Table 3); (3) calendar-month breakdown (Table 4), size-group subsamples with 30/40/30 breakpoints (Table 5), liquidity filters (Table 6), per-country results (Table 7), and risk-factor regressions using self-constructed market/SMB plus French international BM/EP/CEP/DP factors (Tables 8-10), decile-count sensitivity (Table 12). All 12 tables report point estimates with t-statistics. Note: the paper's proprietary FactSet data is unavailable in our catalog; Stage 5 will verify a documented substitute (Compustat Global daily + Compustat North America for Canada, USD conversion via Compustat Global FX), making this a data-substitution replication targeting Tier 1 where possible and Tier 2 (pattern-level) where the vintage gap bites.
